title: Vibe Coding Is The Only Future - Steve Yegge
summary: Interview with Steve Yegge on his career and 'Vibe Coding' book: CLI agents over IDEs, engineers as team leads for agents, modularity, taste.

assertions.quote: now claims he can write 12,000 lines of production code per day using AI agents

verdicts.note: Lines of code isn't a productivity measure, and controlled studies show modest gains; sustained output of that size without proportional review implies unreviewed code.

One cited case (claudes-c-compiler) shows ~500K lines added by Claude over a few weeks, so tens of thousands of lines per day are possible, but nothing here establishes that this is production-quality code or attributes it to experienced engineers.

assertions.quote: if you're using cursor right now and you probably love it right you're using like last year's technology

verdicts.note: IDE products added full agents, background agents and CLIs of their own; usage data show both forms widely used. Many experts (e.g. Karpathy) argue visual diff UIs are key for verification.

assertions.quote: it will fill the entire context window with that task ... and start making panicked decisions

verdicts.note: Long-context benchmarks (e.g. NoLiMa, context-rot studies) show degradation as context grows; the exact threshold is model-dependent.

assertions.quote: you have to decompose tasks into the smallest possible conceptual move forward

verdicts.note: Small batches with fast feedback are a strong DORA predictor of delivery performance; DORA 2024 linked AI to larger batches and lower stability.

assertions.quote: you're not a programmer anymore. You're a ... team lead

verdicts.note: Background and parallel agents are increasingly used, but most developers still work interactively with one agent; enterprise adoption of orchestration is early.
The review documents a role shift toward supervising and validating AI output. Multi-agent orchestration specifically is barely studied.

assertions.quote: you're responsible for the outcomes and you can't ever blame the AI for anything

verdicts.note: Given documented defect and security rates in AI code, human review before merge is standard practice (e.g. Amazon's two-person rule for AI-assisted changes); it's a sound norm.
The paper recommends careful review of AI code whatever the tool, along with static analysis, tests, security checks, and monitoring after merge.

assertions.quote: modularity sits at the heart of it ... If it's too big of a monolith ... it can't do any thinking at all

verdicts.note: Clear module boundaries help both humans and agents navigate and test; consistent with Ousterhout and practitioner reports.

assertions.quote: the people with taste are the ones ... because the difficulty of producing it is going to go so far down

verdicts.note: Plausible economic logic and widely argued, but not measured; execution, distribution and maintenance still matter.

assertions.quote: people need to stop talking about code being the bottleneck and typing typing was never the bottleneck ... they're misdirecting the conversation

verdicts.note: Studies of developer time show coding is a minority of work; DORA and Faros 2025 found individual coding gains often don't translate into delivery throughput.

assertions.quote: these $200 a month ... those are all loss leaders

verdicts.note: Heavy users clearly consume more compute than flat fees cover, which is why vendors added weekly limits; whether plans are below cost on average is not public.

assertions.quote: It doesn't typically lie about what it does, right? But it grossly exaggerates the impact of what it does

verdicts.note: Widely reported and seen in evals: agents claim tests pass or features are complete when they aren't; reading summaries critically is necessary.
